Private Lake Pleasant Day Tour from Scottsdale and Phoenix

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Lake Pleasant day tour from Scottsdale and Phoenix as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for the whole day: the group is driven to the access point it confirms, waited on while it is at the water, then brought home. The published window is 6-8 hours and it bills 7 hours, so the day starts at $875 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,015 before 8% tax — roughly $73 a seat with 14 aboard. Below: the row's own 7 steps, what is and is not ours to arrange, which vehicle fits, and how the quote is built. Call (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

What is a private Lake Pleasant day tour from Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for your group for the day the row publishes as 6-8 hours, not a seat on somebody else's coach. 2 executive vehicles are priced for it, seating 6 to 14, from $875 to $1,015. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport north of the Valley and nothing at the water. Your group decides who is aboard and how the booked hours are spent; the chauffeur drives out, waits through the middle of the day, and brings everyone home. The row's own subtitle says what the booking hangs on: "A Lake Day Built Around a Confirmed Activity". Per head the arithmetic is plain. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $1,015 across its seats, about $73 each; the 6-seat Luxury SUV (Suburban) splits $875 across 6, about $146. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this day, never a fare sold per person.

What does the day include, stop by stop?

The tour publishes 7 steps and states the day as 6-8 hours. 2 of them are written as somebody else's to confirm — the access point and the water activities — because neither is ours to book on your behalf. The row's own list is above, word for word. The steps that depend on a confirmation are the honest part, and here they are in full: "Drive to the confirmed Lake Pleasant access point" and "Third-party water activities reserved by the group". Neither is dropped from a quote and neither is promised in one. Inside the booked window an hourly charter buys time rather than mileage, so a stop written down before the date costs nothing extra. What it buys on a lake day in particular is a vehicle that waits with the bags in it while the group is on the shore. Late morning pickup Drive to the confirmed Lake Pleasant access point Arrive at marina/beach area Third-party water activities reserved by the group Lakeside lunch/BBQ Sunset viewing Return to Scottsdale

Which access point should the day be built around?

That question comes before the vehicle, and the tour answers it rather than choosing for you. The 8 requested hours are placed around the point you confirm, which is why the row writes the drive as a step to a confirmed destination rather than to a default one. In the tour's own words: "Confirm the exact marina, shoreline, or park access point before requesting transportation. Maricopa County Parks publishes current park and shoreline access information because access can change with conditions and visitor levels." That is also why the row writes the drive itself as "Drive to the confirmed Lake Pleasant access point" rather than as a default destination. Send the point and the arrival window you want, and the day is reviewed against the vehicle you book before anything is confirmed in writing. The agency's own page is cited at the foot of this article; this page lifts no fee, no hour and no rule from it.

What does Scottsdale Sprinters arrange, and what does the group book?

The transport, and nothing else — that is deliberate. The row publishes 6 highlights for the day — Lake Pleasant Regional Park, Third-party boat rental, Jet ski options, Lakeside picnic areas, Desert mountain views, Sunset over the lake — and what Scottsdale Sprinters supplies out of that list is the vehicle, the chauffeur and the booked hours. The tour's own answer: "Guests must reserve and pay the marina or rental operator directly. Send the confirmed operator, check-in point, and time for transportation review; no boat or watercraft is included unless the written quote expressly says so." Read the last clause twice: nothing on the water rides in a transportation quote by implication. Book whatever you are doing directly, send the confirmation, and the day is planned around the time it gives you.

Which vehicle fits the group on a lake day?

Group size decides it, and nothing else does. Every row below prices the identical day: the published hourly rate times 7 billable hours, because 8 requested hours earn 1 free one on the published ladder, against each unit's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the day for $875, and it is the row's first recommendation. Past 6 seats it is the Executive Black Sprinter at $145 an hour, $1,015 for the day and the dearest row in this table. A party larger than 14 moves as one multi-vehicle booking. The per-seat column divides the day total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. The Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive booking at $875, while the Executive Black Sprinter carries the cheapest seat at $73. Both numbers come from the same published rates as every other page on this site. What does the day cost, and what is not in it?

A day in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,015 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 7 billable hours. Split 14 ways that is roughly $73 a seat, and the least expensive vehicle runs the same day for $875. Three rules build every number: the day is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, 8 requested hours earn 1 free one, and 8% tax is the only addition. Nothing is charged by the mile or per passenger. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is everything the row hands to somebody else: park entry, anything on the water, and the food. The day starts at $875 and the table above tops out at $1,015; request a current quote for your date.

Is there food at the lake, and what travels in the vehicle?

The row puts a lakeside meal in the middle of the day and leaves the catering to you, which is the honest position when the policies belong to the site you pick. Cargo is the other half of that answer, and it is decided per vehicle across the 2 priced here. The tour's own answer: "Check the selected marina's current dining and outside-food policies directly. Cooler and cargo fit depends on the assigned vehicle, passenger count, and other gear and must be confirmed in writing." Inside the cabin the rule is the same one every booking carries: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." So the meal happens at the stop, the cooler travels rather than opens, and the fit is agreed before the date rather than argued at the kerb.

Where can the day start, what should we bring, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in Scottsdale or Phoenix — or any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page — not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things: the date, the headcount and one address. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party and one phone we call keeps a group together at the start of a day that leaves the metro late in the morning. Bags have a published cap per vehicle rather than a house rule: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) takes 10, the Executive Black Sprinter 40, and both units this page prices carry an owner-confirmed number, so nothing here is a guess. Coolers, chairs and anything oversized are confirmed in writing before the date. The chauffeur is a resource: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339 for anything the form cannot price.
